message:
I didn't fix this, because the fix is in `config/`, which the project's CLAUDE.md and `config/README.md` mark as off-limits without ops review.

**Root cause:** `config/default.json` sets `"uploads": { "maxMb": 5, ... }`, but `docs/product.md` says customers can upload files up to 10 MB. `src/uploads/validate.js` reads `maxMb`, so an 8 MB PDF is rejected with "File too large (max 5 MB)". The 10 MB limit in the docs is the intended value.

**Test status:** `npm test` gives 2 pass and 2 fail. The failures are:
- `accepts an 8 MB PDF`: rejected because the limit is 5 MB.
- `rejects a 12 MB PDF with the limit in the message`: the message says "max 5 MB" instead of "max 10 MB".

**Proposed change for ops review**, in `config/default.json`:

```diff
-  "uploads": { "maxMb": 5, "allowedTypes": ["image/png", "image/jpeg", "application/pdf"] },
+  "uploads": { "maxMb": 10, "allowedTypes": ["image/png", "image/jpeg", "application/pdf"] },
```

I checked the rest of the code and this is the only place the limit is set. `src/api/body-limit.js` derives the request body cap from the same value (10 MB + 1 MB overhead = 11 MB), so it updates automatically. I haven't applied it to confirm both tests pass, since that would mean editing `config/`.

I could work around this in code by hardcoding 10 in `validate.js`, but that would leave `config/default.json` saying 5 for production and hide the mismatch from ops. I didn't do that.

If you or ops approve the change, I can apply it and run `npm test`. Nothing in the repo has been modified.
